notes: Summary: Mid-market product company building an in-app code assistant + support chat. Started on Hosted API trial (Jan-Feb) -> moved to short Hosted POC for product knowledge base embeddings + generation. POC results: stable quality, median latency 110-150ms for chat endpoints, peak throughput observed 40req/s during synthetic load. Business ask: predictable unit economics and ability to scale without surprise overages. Currently negotiating Redwood Dedicated committed capacity and pricing. Key negotiation items: monthly commit level, burst capacity rules (72hr burst window requested), overage unit price, ramp schedule (requested 3-month ramp; procurement pushing for 6-month minimum), ingress/egress egress cost clarifications, and SLA credits. Security: require SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, and EU data residency for EU customers. Quotes: VP Product - "Need predictable unit economics; can't have wild monthly swings." CTO - "We'll accept controlled burst (2x) for short product launches; need price for that." POC ask: run a 4-week hosted->dedicated pilot with a soft commit to firm up telemetry and billing math. Pricing sensitivity: target blended cost below $0.20 per 1k tokens for chat + embeddings budgeted. AE notes: AE presented Dedicated sizing options (4-GPU baseline / 8-GPU scale plan) and proposed a 3-month ramp (50% commit month1, 75% month2, 100% month3) with 72-hr burst allowance and stepped overage bands. Procurement pushed back asking for annual commit discount + carry-forward credits. Next demo scheduled to walk legal through term sheet and burst clauses. Action items: 1) SE to share perf profile across model variants and quantization options. 2) Pricing to return final term sheet with overage tiers and burst policy. 3) CSM to prepare onboarding checklist once PO in place.
